title: Good Subsequence Queries
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer p, a non-empty subsequence of nums is considered good if its length is strictly less than n and the greatest common divisor (GCD) of its elements is exactly p.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer p, a non-empty subsequence of nums is considered good if its length is strictly less than n and the greatest common divisor (GCD) of its elements is exactly p. After each query that updates nums[indi] to vali, determine whether there exists any good subsequence in the current array. Return the count of queries for which a good subsequence exists.
constraints: nums is nonempty, p is positive, and each query [index,value] updates nums permanently.
A good subsequence is nonempty, proper, and has gcd exactly p.
Return how many post-update arrays contain at least one good subsequence.
hints: Only values divisible by p can participate; their total gcd must be p for any qualifying subset.
Maintain their gcd under updates with a segment tree and track how many are divisible.
If some array element is excluded already, the full divisible set is proper. If all qualify, test deleting one element; for n>6 the gcd witness always has a proper subset.
Adding divisible values cannot change gcd p away from p, so any smaller witness extends to one of these maximal proper subsets.
editorial: Adding divisible values cannot change gcd p away from p, so any smaller witness extends to one of these maximal proper subsets.

tests.explanation: After the first update no divisible subset has gcd two; after the second, [6,16] does, so one query qualifies.
The only nonempty subsequence is the full length-one array and is not proper, so the count is zero.
